title: The abstract equivalence theorem
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,F)$ be a Galois category in the sense of [def-galois-category] and
$G=\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ with the topology of [def-galois-category]. Write $\text{finite-}G\text{-}\mathbf{Sets}$ for the category whose objects are finite sets $E$ with a left action of $G$ such that the action map $G\times E\to E$ is continuous for the discrete topology on $E$, and whose morphisms are the $G$-equivariant maps. Then the functor
$\mathcal C\to \text{finite-}G\text{-}\mathbf{Sets}$, $X\mapsto F(X)$ with the induced action $\gamma\cdot x=\gamma_X(x)$, $f\mapsto F(f)$, is an equivalence of categories.

proof.text: From [def-galois-category] install finite limits and finite colimits on C, and exactness and conservativity of F composed with FintypeCat.incl. Because the inclusion reflects finite limits and colimits, Mathlib preservesFiniteLimits_of_reflects_of_preserves and preservesFiniteColimits_of_reflects_of_preserves transfer exactness to F. Reflection of isomorphisms transfers by reflectsIsomorphisms_of_comp.

proof.text: [lem-galois-axioms](2) makes each epi fibre-surjective. ConcreteCategory.epi_of_surjective therefore proves F.PreservesEpimorphisms. The remaining FiberFunctor fields follow from exactness and conservativity; preservation of finite group quotients is transported after shrinking the group just as in the preceding step. This constructs FiberFunctor F with no additional hypotheses.
